findings.claim: In 2026, the official average or typical XAUUSD spreads that the main raw-spread brokers publish fall at about $0.08-0.12/oz: IC Markets EU 0.08 (min 0.00), IC Markets Global 0.09 (min 0.05), Tickmill EU 0.09 typical (min 0.08), FP Markets about 0.09-0.10 (undated), and Pepperstone Razor 0.12 average (min 0.08) for 1-31 Aug 2026, when gold closed between $4,333 and $4,680.

Adding fixed per-lot commissions of $4.50-7.00 round trip ($0.045-0.07/oz on a 100-oz lot) puts the all-in round-trip cost on these accounts at about $0.13-0.19/oz, or $13-19 per lot. For comparison: Pepperstone Standard averaged $0.25/oz in Aug 2026; Admirals is about $0.46/oz on Zero.MT5 and $0.49/oz on Trade.MT5; Darwinex is about $0.50/oz.

On MT4/MT5, the fixed per-lot commission is the same for gold as for FX at these brokers: IC Markets (USD 3.50/side; EUR 3.25 for EUR accounts), Pepperstone (USD 3.50/side; EUR 2.60), Tickmill ($3), FP Markets ($3), Fusion ($2.25), Vantage ($3 for precious metals) and Admirals ($3.0; EUR 2.6). A 100-oz gold lot is worth about $400k+ at current prices, so on these accounts the commission is tiny relative to notional.

At some brokers the gold commission differs from FX or scales with the gold price. Figures are per 100-oz lot at gold $4,065.62: Darwinex charges 0.0025%/side of notional (about $20.33 RT). RoboForex ECN charges 20 USD per $1M per side (about $16.26 RT) and RoboForex/RoboMarkets Prime 10/$1M (about $8.13 RT). Dukascopy charges metals 52.5 USD/$1M per side vs 35 for FX at deposits under $5k (about $46.75 RT on MT4, $42.69 on JForex). IC Markets cTrader/TradingView charge $3 per $100k per side (about $24.39 RT). Pepperstone cTrader charges $7 RT on XAU/USD vs $6 on FX. Exness charges $5.5/side on XAUUSD in the Zero account vs 'from $0.05' on FX, and $3.5/side on Raw ('up to $3.5' for FX).

Pepperstone moved Razor gold to a raw spread plus commission model in mid-2026 (Razor Gold guide published 18 Jun 2026). Before that, XAUUSD had identical spreads on Razor and Standard with no commission: min 0.05 / avg 0.18 in Jul 2024 at gold about $2,400, and avg 0.25 in the EU Costs & Charges doc v07/2025. Now Razor is avg 0.12 + $7 RT, about $0.19/oz all-in, vs Standard 0.25, which matches Pepperstone's claim that total cost is 'broadly unchanged'.

Dollar spreads on raw accounts have risen much less than the gold price. Tickmill's typical XAUUSD spread was 0.07 on 12 Mar 2020 (gold $1,576.88) and is 0.09 in 2026 (gold about $4,066 on 4 Nov 2026). BrokersView measured IC Markets at 6.6 points in Jun 2024 (gold month-end $2,325) and 10.4 points in Feb 2026 (gold $4,704-5,279), i.e. about $0.066 to $0.104/oz.

Measured gold spreads have large tails. BrokersView recorded IC Markets' worst XAUUSD spread at 746 points (about $7.46) against a 10.4-point average in Feb 2026. In Jun 2024 the maxima were 50 points for IC Markets and 491 for Tickmill. Averages that include rollover (Pepperstone's do) are more conservative than 'typical' figures.

At $4,000+ gold, overnight swaps are large compared with trading costs; holding a long one night costs several times a full round trip of spread and commission (about $13-19 per lot). IC Markets EU XAUUSD: long -52.217 points (about -$52/lot/night) vs short +36. RoboForex/RoboMarkets: long -60 pips (-$60) vs short +19. Vantage on 3 Sep 2026: long -$80.54 vs short +$32.67 per lot per night, with a Wednesday triple of about -$241.62. Admirals: long -0.01738% vs short +0.00496%.

For a French retail trader, EU-regulated commission-based gold on MetaTrader is available from: IC Markets (EU) Ltd (CySEC 362/18), Pepperstone EU Ltd (CySEC 388/20), Tickmill Europe Ltd, FP Markets (EU-facing pages), RoboMarkets Ltd (Prime; CySEC 191/13), Admirals Europe Ltd (Zero.MT5; CySEC 201/13), Darwinex via Sapiens Markets EU (CNMV reg. 311) and Dukascopy Europe IBS AS (MT4 rates published, MT5 not). EUR-base accounts pay fixed EUR commissions, which are lower in nominal terms than the USD rates: IC Markets EU EUR 3.25/side (EUR 6.50 RT), Pepperstone EU EUR 2.60/side (EUR 5.20 RT), Admirals EUR 2.6/side (EUR 5.20 RT), and FP Markets EUR 2.75/side per third-party tables.

sweeps.caveats: 1) Many official pages do not date their figures or explain how averages are computed: IC Markets, Tickmill, FP Markets, RoboForex/RoboMarkets, Admirals and Darwinex give MIN/AVG or 'typical' with no window. Only Pepperstone states a window (1-31 Aug 2026, all sessions including rollover). The RoboForex averages look static or indicative. 2) Some sites blocked direct reading, so their figures come from search-result extracts and are lower confidence: FP Markets, Vantage and the Exness help center returned HTTP 403, Darwinex's spreads page loops on redirects, and the try.tickmill.com host did not resolve in this sandbox (www.tickmill.com was used instead). The FP Markets metals averages may be several years old. 3) Pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, so verify any figure against the live MT5 symbol specification before relying on it. 4) Units: on these MT5 gold symbols 1 point = $0.01/oz, and brokers loosely call the same thing 'pips', 'points' or cents. Values were read as USD/oz because a gold tick is $0.01. 5) Notional-based commissions (Darwinex, Dukascopy, RoboForex/RoboMarkets, IC cTrader) were computed at gold $4,065.62 (StatMuse close, 4 Nov 2026), assuming a 100-oz lot and the same open and close price. They scale linearly with the gold price. 6) Commissions for EUR accounts are EUR-denominated and were not converted to USD, since no sourced EURUSD rate was used. 7) BrokersView/FastBull measurements are third-party, from the Singapore market, with the account type unspecified. 8) Swap figures change daily; the Vantage figures are a single-day snapshot from a Standard STP account. 9) Whether French residents can join the offshore entities (Fusion, Vantage, Exness offshore, RoboForex Ltd) was not verified; they lack EU protections, while EU entities cap retail gold leverage at 1:20. 10) Gold prices come from StatMuse, an aggregator.

findings.claim: ESMA's 2018 product intervention, applied to CFDs from 1 Aug 2018, capped retail leverage at '20:1 for non-major currency pairs, gold and major indices'. It standardised margin close-out 'at 50% of minimum required margin' per account and required negative balance protection per account.

In France, the AMF's national decision of 1 Aug 2019 (MiFIR art. 42) replaced ESMA's temporary measure and 'shall apply until it is revoked'. Annex I sets initial margin at 5% of notional for gold, i.e. max 20:1. Close-out applies when account funds plus unrealised P&L fall 'to less than half of the total initial margin protection'. Negative balance protection limits liability to the funds in the CFD account. Incentives are banned and a provider-specific loss-percentage risk warning is mandatory.

These protections are retail-only. IG France: negative balance protection 'n'est pas applicable aux clients professionnels'. Tickmill EU lists XAUUSD max leverage 1:20 for retail vs 1:500 for professional clients.

findings.claim: Triple-swap day for spot gold (XAUUSD) is Wednesday at nearly every broker checked, because spot gold settles T+2 like FX. IC Markets: 'On Wednesday night swaps for FX, Metals, Bonds and CFDs on Commodities are charged a triple rate'. Admirals GOLD: '3-day SWAPs: Wednesday'. RoboMarkets XAUUSD: '3-days swap Wednesday'. Tickmill: FX pairs, gold and silver tripled on Wednesday, all other instruments on Friday. XM: Wednesday for forex and spot metals, Friday for cash indices, energies and stocks. OANDA: gold and silver CFDs are T+2, so weekend financing is applied on Wednesday. Blueberry: metals on Wednesday, other instruments on Friday. Pepperstone: tripled on the Wednesday-Thursday rollover, with a caveat that it can vary by asset class.

Exceptions to the Wednesday rule. QNB Invest's 2019 XAUUSD notices put the 3-day charge on Thursday, while its 2020 notices say Wednesday. Born2trade's 2026 gold promotion used a multiplier of 1 on every weekday, with no triple. Friday triple swaps are the convention for indices, energies and stocks, not spot gold. Always check the '3-days swap' field in the MT5 symbol specification.

Theory: the gold forward premium (GOFO) equals the USD interest rate minus the gold lease rate. The fair rollover carry is therefore about -(USD rate - lease rate) per year for a long spot-gold position and about +(USD rate - lease rate) for a short. Brokers then subtract a markup from both sides. GOFO, and hence the forward premium, has at times been negative, for example in late 2008.

Broker method A passes through the liquidity provider's tom-next or forward rate, which already embeds the lease rate, plus an admin fee. OANDA: providers' tom-next swap rates plus a 1% admin fee on both long and short gold/silver CFDs, charged daily on a /365 basis. Admirals: provider annual rate minus a 2% admin fee, with daily = annual/360. Its worked gold example uses provider rates of -4.21% long / +3.712% short, giving -6.21% / +1.712% p.a. and, for 1 lot at $3,992.66, -$68.87 / +$18.99 per night (example date unknown). IG: tom-next rate plus an admin fee.

Broker method B uses a USD benchmark only and ignores the lease rate, which is why gold and silver get identical % rates. TMS / OANDA TMS: long = -(SOFR + margin), short = SOFR - margin, with a GOLD/SILVER margin of 1.80% in 2024 to March 2026 and about 3.00% implied from July/August 2026. In 2018 it was the USD 1-week deposit ± 0.35% (.pro) or 0.65% (.std). XTB: long = SOFR + margin, short = margin - SOFR, and shorts are never credited. XTB's implied gold margin was about 11.4% (Feb 2026) and 8.4% (Apr 2026), against 4.5% for its other commodities.

The base rate implied by the TMS gold swaps, (short - long)/2, follows the USD policy cycle: 5.31% (Jan 2024), 5.33% (Jun 2024), 4.85% (Oct 2024), 4.36% (Mar 2025), 4.20% (Oct 2025), 3.64-3.65% (Jan to Aug 2026), 3.85% (21 Sep 2026) and 3.94% (2 Nov 2026). The last two follow the FOMC hike to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026. The long cost is about this base plus margin, and the short credit about this base minus margin. (My calculation from the published tables.)

The London 1-month gold lease rate is normally near zero but spiked in early 2025. BullionVault: 0.08% on 2 Jan 2025 (November 2024 average 0.08%, December 2024 average 0.49%), 5.7% in the week before 10 Feb 2025, then 3.72% on 10 Feb 2025, with a COMEX premium of about $25/oz. Under method A a higher lease rate shrinks both the long cost and the short credit. Under method B (TMS, XTB) it has no effect.

Implied carry at provider-priced MT brokers can sit well away from SOFR (my calculation). Vantage and IC Markets in November 2024 implied about 3.6% against SOFR of about 4.6-4.8%, i.e. an embedded gold rate of about 1%. IC Markets EU (16 Jan 2026 table) implies about 4.9% against SOFR of about 3.6%, which produces an unusually large short credit (+4.5% p.a.). In November 2026, RoboMarkets implies about 3.5%, Admirals about 4.0% and Capital.com about 4.1%.

Typical 2023-2026 levels (22 long and 17 short data points, excluding XTB and promotions). Long: median about -5.9% p.a., range about -4.2% to -7.9%. Short: median about +2.4% p.a., range about +0.65% to +4.5%. Short credits were largest when SOFR was about 5.3% (2024: +3.0% to +3.5%) and shrank in 2026 (+0.65% to +2.6%) as rates fell and some margins rose. Exceptions: TMS in October 2023 was negative on both sides (-3.63% / -3.51%) despite 5.3% USD rates; XTB charges -12% to -15% long and -5% to -8% short. In USD at 2026 prices of $4,100-4,400, a 1-lot long costs about $57-96 per night, about three times that on Wednesday.

Low-rate era (2015-2020 data; nothing found for 2013-2014 or 2021). With USD rates at about 0-1%, carry was near zero and the markup dominated, so both sides were usually negative. TMS Trader 2015-2017: long -3.4% to -3.8%, short -2.3% to -2.8%, with a markup of about 3%. QNB November 2019: -3.76% / -1.50% and -3.72% / 0%. QNB October 2020: -1.92% / 0%. When USD rates were about 2% (2018), a low-markup account charged about -2.4% long and paid about +1.6% short (TMS Prime). Typical: long about -2% to -4% (median about -3.5%), short about -3% to 0% (median about -1.5%). In USD terms that was only about $10-15 per lot per night at $1,100-1,900 gold.

Units seen across brokers. IC Markets: swaps 'calculated in points', which MT4/5 converts to account currency; for 2-digit XAUUSD and 100 oz, 1 point is about $1 per lot. RoboMarkets: 'pips' with a pip size of 0.01, also $1 per lot. Admirals: % per day (annual/360). Capital.com and XTB: % per day. TMS/OANDA TMS: % per annum on an ACT/360 basis. Annual % of notional ≈ per-night USD per lot x 365 / (100 x gold price), because the triple Wednesday covers the weekend.

sweeps.caveats: 1) Live pages (Admirals, Capital.com, RoboMarkets) are undated, so I used the fetch date (2026-11-05) and the pricegold.net price for that day ($4,126.22, captured midday New York). The IC Markets EU swap page carries a 16 Jan 2026 byline but may be updated live, so both conversions are shown. 2) The TMS Trader 2015-2017 tables say only 'values in pips'. I assumed 1 XAUUSD pip = $0.10/oz. With that assumption the implied carry tracks the Fed hikes (0.31% → 0.42% → 0.52% → 0.75%), whereas $0.01 would imply an implausible 0.03-0.08%. Gold and silver also carry identical % rates under it. For TMS Prime 2018 I assumed a $0.01 minimum step, which reproduces the stated 0.35% margin. 3) The Investing.com/Vantage November 2024 figures have no stated units; I assumed USD per 100-oz lot. Entities were not stated and look like offshore/global 1000:1 accounts. The ForexBenchmark/Finance Magnates figures (3 Sep 2026) give long swaps only, mostly for unspecified entities. 4) Annualization: per-night USD x 365 / (100 oz x price). Published %/day x 365 for Capital.com and XTB. Admirals nominal = x360, effective = x365. The TMS % p.a. figures are ACT/360, so their effective cost is about 1.4% larger in relative terms (e.g. -6.94% → -7.04%). 5) Gold prices come from pricegold.net (benchmark not stated), Reuters via Finance Magnates ($4,409.97 on 3 Sep 2026; pricegold shows $4,467.77), LBMA PM via an SDBullion search extract (18 Jan 2016) and the September 2015 monthly average (no daily figure found). 6) QNB Invest is a Turkish broker (not EU) and its platform was not checked; it is included only for 2019-2020 low-rate evidence. XTB is not MT5 (xStation) and is included only as a French-market comparator. Whether OANDA TMS and Capital.com offer MT5 was not checked. 7) Blocked or unreachable: myfxbook, BrokerChooser, afterprime.com, help.afterprime.com, VT Markets help, web.archive.org (so no archived spec pages), and xm.com (the XM triple-day rule comes from a search extract). help.admiralmarkets.com would not resolve and would need to be allowed in this session's network settings; I read the same article on admirals.freshdesk.com instead. I got no live swap tables for Pepperstone EU, Exness, Tickmill, FxPro, FP Markets or Vantage EU. 8) No data was found for 2013-2014 or for 2021-2022. October 2023 (TMS) and January 2024 stand in for the 2023 rate environment. FastBull/BrokersView 'average swap' figures (e.g. IC Markets -8.74 USD/lot in Nov 2025 and -10.65 in Dec 2025) were not used because their method is undefined and they give no long/short split. 9) The implied carry/markup splits and the medians are my own calculations from the published rows, not broker statements. The IC Markets EU short credit of about +4.5% to +5% p.a. is an outlier that could not be cross-checked.

Bar-based studies and M1-OHLC backtests therefore understate rollover and news widening. For example, a published dataset of MT5 M5 bars (Aug 2025-Jul 2026, one unnamed raw account, symbol XAUUSDm) reports a median spread of $0.16 'identical in all 24 hours', while the tick data above show 3-10x widening at rollover and news.

sweeps.caveats:
1) Several key numbers are my own calculations from third-party copies of tick data, not figures published by brokers.
- Dukascopy: Hugging Face 'Henrik404/dukascopy-ticks', converted from 'mito0o852/dukascopy-ticks'. Dukascopy's own datafeed host reset connections from this environment, so it could not be read directly.
- Tickmill: an MT5 tick export labelled Tickmill on Hugging Face ('Snail000/Tickmill-XAUUSD-Ticks'). The account type and legal entity are not stated. I assumed the server clock is New York time + 7h and checked this by matching prices with Dukascopy (mean gap $0.075 at UTC+3 vs $9.75 at UTC+2).
- The prices are consistent with the real gold path (Dukascopy's Jan 2026 maximum mid of $5,598 vs a reported all-time high of $5,597.69).
- Method: each quote is weighted by how long it stood; quotes lasting more than 600 s are treated as market closed. Hours are New York local time. For news events, the baseline is 60 to 5 minutes before the release, the 'first minute' is the minute after it, and the maximum is the widest tick from 10 seconds before to 2 minutes after.

2) Coverage gaps:
- Dukascopy was sampled for March and October of 2016-2025, plus Aug/Nov 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026.
- The mirror starts in 2016, so 2013-2015 is not covered, and it ends in March 2026.
- web.archive.org could not be reached, so archived broker spread tables from 2013-2021 could not be checked.
- OANDA's historical spreads tool is interactive and was not used.

3) Maximum spreads in both tick feeds cluster just below round values (Dukascopy about $2, $3, $6 and $15 in different periods; Tickmill about $2.5-3.0). This suggests the feeds cap spreads, so true extremes may be larger.

4) Saxo does not define its XAUUSD 'pip'. The USD conversions assume 1 pip = $0.01, inferred from its tolerance buckets; if Saxo's pip is $0.10, multiply those USD figures by 10.

5) Dukascopy's quotes come from its own marketplace and may not match what a Dukascopy Europe MT5 account shows. Its commissions are tiered, based on notional value, and come from an undated fee page.

6) Broker slippage statistics (FXCM, XTB, Admirals) cover all instruments, are self-reported and use different definitions. Pepperstone's and Exness's figures are marketing claims. No gold stop-slippage statistics were found for Pepperstone, IC Markets or Tickmill.

7) FXEmpire's spreads are single snapshots. The BrokersView and BestBrokers averages do not disclose their methods, and their 'pip' values were converted assuming 1 pip = $0.01. The Oct 2026 gold price (~$4,145) comes from a secondary aggregator. FXCM's March 2020 Active Trader figure (15.7 pips) looks anomalous but is reported as published.

8) The news samples are small (5-8 events per type and period), and only one ECN feed (Tickmill) is measured. A French retail client would be served by an EU entity (CySEC or Latvia), whose conditions may differ from the global or UK pages cited.

9) Scripts and output files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/scripts/ and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/out/ (monthly.csv, hourly.csv, minutes.csv, events.csv).

synthesis.lab_model_verdict:
Basis: cost per round trip at $4,000, both fills at market or stop, swap excluded.

LAB MODEL: $0.60 Dukascopy spread (1.5 bp) + 2 x $0.60 slippage (1.5 bp per side) + $0.07 commission = $1.87/oz (4.7 bp).

PER SCENARIO:
- vs low_cost_ecn ($0.59): the lab is CONSERVATIVE by $1.28/oz (3.2x). That is +$0.48 on spread (Dukascopy's quote is 5-10x a raw ECN quote) and +$0.80 on slippage.
- vs typical_retail ($1.16): the lab is CONSERVATIVE by $0.71/oz (1.6x). That is +$0.24 on spread, +$0.40 on slippage and +$0.07 on commission.
- vs conservative ($2.47): the lab is OPTIMISTIC by $0.60/oz; it covers only 76%. That is -$0.20 on spread and -$0.40 on slippage. The pre-registered x1.5 stress ($2.81) covers this case.
- If the exit is a limit/target fill, remove one side of slippage: lab $1.27, low $0.39, typical $0.76, conservative $1.67.
- The ordering is the same at IS-era prices (about $1,300, sim-implied): lab about $0.75 vs about $0.26 / $0.43 / $0.98.

PLAIN VERDICT: the lab model is mildly conservative overall. It is clearly conservative for a good EU raw-spread account, and conservative for a typical EU standard account in normal conditions. It is about right as 'typical retail with mediocre stop fills'. It is not a worst case.

THREE QUALIFICATIONS:
1. The margin is thinner than it looks for stop-entry and trailing-stop strategies. Against Dukascopy ticks, the M1 engine flatters donch4h_stop by $0.574 per trade (/home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/audit/trend__donch4h_stop.json). That is about half of its $1.12-per-trade slippage budget, leaving about 0.75 bp per side for real execution loss: still more than low-cost, about equal to typical, and short of the bad-fills case.
2. The $0.07 commission is right for fixed-per-lot brokers (IC, Pepperstone, Tickmill, FP, Admirals) but optimistic for notional-commission accounts. At Dukascopy Europe itself (MT4 table, under $5k equity), commission is about $0.46/oz round trip at $4,000, so the lab model would be optimistic by about $0.39/oz there.
3. Swap per oz per night at $4,000:
   - Longs: lab $0.56 vs $0.51 (low), $0.67 (typical), $0.89 (conservative). About right; slightly optimistic vs typical and conservative.
   - Shorts: the lab charges $0.22 vs $0 / $0.17 / $0.33 in the sample-safe scenarios, while EU brokers currently credit shorts about $0.10-0.35 per night. So the lab is conservative on shorts today.
   - For a 2-night long at $4,000, the lab's swap (about $1.11) is as large as a whole typical-retail round trip. For multi-day strategies, swap, not spread, is the cost item to get right.
synthesis.eu_retail_constraints:
FRENCH / EU RETAIL CFD RULES. ESMA's 2018 product intervention was made permanent in France by the AMF decision of 1 Aug 2019 (MiFIR art. 42), in force until revoked:
- Gold initial margin is 5% of notional, i.e. at most 20:1.
- Positions are closed out when equity falls below 50% of the required initial margin, per account.
- Negative balance protection applies per CFD account.
- Bonuses and incentives are banned, and a standardised loss-percentage risk warning is mandatory.
- Sapin II (art. L.533-12-7 CMF) restricts online advertising of these products, and the AMF keeps a blacklist of unauthorised Forex/CFD sellers.

BROKERS' GOLD TERMS MATCH THESE RULES. Pepperstone EU 20:1; XTB 5% / 20:1; IG France 5%; Swissquote EU 5% (1:20); Admirals retail 5%; Dukascopy Europe leverage 20 with margin call at 100% and stop-out at 50%; RoboMarkets Prime fixed 1:20.

PROTECTIONS ARE RETAIL-ONLY. Opting up to professional status removes them: Tickmill EU allows 1:500 for professionals, and IG France states that negative balance protection does not apply to professional clients.

SIZING CHECK. One lot (100 oz) at $4,000 is $400k notional and needs $20k margin; 0.01 lot (1 oz) needs $200. Leverage does not bind fixed-%-risk sizing with ATR stops, but the 50% close-out can liquidate a position whose stop is wide relative to equity.

MT5 FOR A FRENCH RESIDENT, VIA EU ENTITIES:
- Pepperstone EU (CySEC 388/20).
- IC Markets (EU) Ltd (CySEC 362/18; MT5 'recommended').
- Tickmill Europe (CySEC 278/15; ACPR-registered).
- Admirals Europe (CySEC 201/13; Trade.MT5 and Zero.MT5).
- FxPro (CySEC 078/07). Its newer MT5 Raw+ and Elite accounts may be non-EU only.
- Swissquote Capital Markets (CySEC 422/22).
- Dukascopy Europe (Latvia). MT5 commission is not published.
- RoboMarkets Ltd (CySEC 191/13; Prime on MT5).
- Darwinex, via Sapiens Markets EU (CNMV 311). The CNMV fined it EUR 1.048M in Oct 2026 over client-money safeguarding.

NO MT5:
- XTB: xStation only (MT4 was removed on 19 Apr 2024).
- IG France: MT4 only.
- Saxo France: own platforms only.
- IBKR Ireland: its spot gold is an OTC unallocated derivative, not a CFD, with no negative balance protection. Commission is 1.5 bp per side, about $121 per 100 oz round trip at $4,045.

OFFSHORE ENTITIES. Fusion (VFSC), Vantage, Exness, RoboForex (Belize), IC Markets Global, Pepperstone Bahamas and FxPro Bahamas offer up to 1:500 but without ESMA protections. French residents are normally onboarded by the EU entity, and Exness's CySEC entity takes no retail clients. The scenarios therefore use EU-entity pricing only.

EU-ACCOUNT COST DETAILS:
- EUR-base accounts pay fixed EUR commissions: IC EUR 3.25/side, Pepperstone EUR 2.60, Admirals EUR 2.6, FP EUR 2.75 (third-party tables).
- USD P&L on a EUR account is converted; that conversion cost was not researched.
- Pepperstone rounds commission up to $0.04 per 0.01 lot per side, i.e. $0.08/oz round trip on micro lots.
- Admirals charges the full round-turn commission at opening.
synthesis.time_of_day_notes:
1) DUKASCOPY (the sim's spread source) is nearly flat through the session. From the lab's M1 data (close spread vs the 08:00-11:59 NY mean):
- Asian hours are only 1.05-1.07x in 2016-19, 2022-24 and H2-2025.
- The widest windows are the weekday reopen at 18:00-18:04 NY (1.55x in 2016-19, 1.58x in 2022-24, 1.92x in H2-2025) and the Sunday open (1.56x, 1.77x, 2.60x).
- Tick data put the reopen at $1.14-2.26 in Oct 2025-Mar 2026 and the Sunday open at $3.48 in Mar 2026. 16:59 NY was the single widest minute in 2016-19.
- There are no quotes from 17:00 to 18:00 NY.

2) RAW ECN FEEDS ARE FAR SPIKIER in relative terms. Tickmill MT5 (Aug/Oct/Nov 2025):
- Overlap $0.061-0.074; Asia 1.06-1.49x.
- 16:00-16:59 NY 1.6-3.8x; 16:45-16:56 NY $0.11-0.32. Quotes stop about 16:57 and resume at 18:00 NY.
- Weekday 18:00-18:04 NY $0.55-0.73 (7.7-10.8x); 18:15-18:29 NY $0.13-0.46; Sunday open $0.92-1.35.
- In thin August the spread stayed about $0.44 until 19:00 NY.

3) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SIM. A constant spread_mult keeps Dukascopy's mild profile. At mult 0.2, low_cost_ecn is about 2x too expensive in liquid hours (0.2 x $0.62 = $0.12 vs a measured $0.06-0.07). It is 1.2-4x too cheap at the reopen (about $0.24 vs $0.55-0.73) and at the Sunday open (about $0.32 vs $0.92-1.35). Two ways to fix it:
- Use mult >= 0.5 for 16:45-17:00 and 18:00-18:30 NY on weekdays, and 1.0 for the first 30 minutes after the Sunday open. This reproduces the measured ECN rollover spreads.
- Or have the EA place no pending orders and hold no tight stops in those windows.
- For typical_retail, use >= 1.0 in the same windows.
An in-progress liveexec probe in this repo (/home/user/gold-orb/lab/audit/scratch/donch4h_stop/liveexec/p4b_spike_decomp.out) shows the trailing-stop finalist is exposed: its IS PF falls from 1.35 to 1.16 when exits alone see a x5 spread in 16:50-17:00 NY. A x2 spread over 1-2 h around the break had no effect.

4) NEWS (US 08:30 ET NFP/CPI, 14:00 ET FOMC). On Dukascopy, the first-minute spread is a median 1.2-2.1x the prior hour:
- 2024-26: NFP $0.67 to $1.25, CPI $0.54 to $1.10, FOMC $0.57 to $0.98.
- Maximum ticks were $3.5-5; $11.41 at the 11 Feb 2026 NFP and $14.98 at the 6 Mar 2026 NFP.
- Spreads are back to 1.0-1.2x within 5-15 minutes.
- Tickmill's first minute was $0.24-0.71 (3.4-13.6x), with a maximum of $2.07-2.50. The ECN/Dukascopy ratio at news is about 0.2-0.35, so mult 0.2 is roughly right there. At news the bigger cost is stop-fill slippage.

5) 'LIQUID HOURS' for low_cost_ecn means about 03:00-16:30 NY. Outside it, raw spreads are 1.5-10x the overlap level.

6) SWAP is booked at the 17:00 NY rollover, tripled on Wednesday at IC, Admirals, RoboMarkets, Tickmill, XM, OANDA, Blueberry and Pepperstone (spot gold settles T+2). This matches the sim. There are exceptions (QNB 2019 on Thursday; promo accounts with no triple), so check the '3-days swap' field of the MT5 symbol.

7) MT5 BAR DATA understates spreads. MT5's bar 'spread' is the minimum spread in the bar, so backtests on MT5 bar data understate rollover and news spreads. The lab's Dukascopy bid/ask OHLC does not have this flaw, but a constant multiplier reintroduces part of it.

verification.overall:
UNITS & PLAUSIBILITY verdict: no material unit error in the scenario numbers. The conversions check out against the cited pages (re-read on 5 Nov 2026) and the lab data:
- MT5 points to $/oz;
- per-side to round-trip, per lot of 100 oz (IC $3.50, Pepperstone $3.50 on XAU/USD, Tickmill $3, Admirals Zero $3);
- %/day and points to %/yr on the sim's /360 Wednesday-x3 basis;
- notional commissions (Dukascopy $11.5 per $100k round trip = $0.46/oz at $4,000; IBKR 1.5 bp per side = $121 per 100 oz).
All per-round-trip sums recompute exactly. The lab Dukascopy statistics reproduce from the parquet: 2.17 / 1.72 / 1.53 bp; $0.323 at $1,493; $0.61 in Nov 2025. The Tickmill tick claims also reproduce: median $0.06-0.07, mean $0.07-0.117, and the rollover profile. Gold is about $4,116 today (Capital.com live), so the ~$4,045 used for the swap percentages is close.

Weak spots:
1) Slippage. Saxo's XAUUSD pip is undefined. Under the $0.10 reading, Saxo's average stop slippage is about 1.9 bp, which would make low_cost 0.5 bp and typical 1.0 bp optimistic. The only live raw-ECN data (IC, Mar-Apr 2026) implies at least 0.78 bp per stop-entry fill. Use 0.75 bp as the low-cost base for stop strategies.
2) The proposed USD-only rate-linked swap model is contradicted by TMS's own Oct 2023 gold swaps (-3.63% long, -3.51% short with USD at about 5.3%). That makes the 2013-21 swap backcast unreliable.
3) The cited FXCM article's March 2020 figure ($0.157) was left out, which weakens the 'flat standard dollar spread' argument.
4) typical_retail's $0.36 is at the high end for MT5 EU standard accounts; $0.18-0.32 is measured.
5) Minor: the lab model uses the median Dukascopy spread, but the sim charges the mean (1.65 bp), so the lab model is about $1.93 rather than $1.87.
6) Minor: spread_mult < 1 is implemented as a close-spread shift, which creates crossed quotes in about 6% of bars at 0.2 (neutral on average).
7) Minor: 4.6% long swap fits IC and Tickmill but maybe not Pepperstone EU (UK entity: 7.8%).
8) Minor: XTB's current table gives 12.0% / 4.8%, not up to 15% / 7.9%.
9) Minor: the sim.py comment error is confirmed.
